card.title: The Shattered Crown
card.excerpt: A top-down Zelda-like set in the world of Eldoria, built with Phaser 3 — every sprite and every note of music generated by code. Built for the joy of building.

cover.title: The Shattered Crown
cover.lede: A top-down 2D adventure in the spirit of A Link to the Past, set in the world of Eldoria. Built with Phaser 3, and every piece of it — the pixel art, the chiptune music — is generated by code rather than drawn or recorded. It runs entirely in the browser, and offline.
cover.note: A side project, built for the joy of building rather than to ship anything. The art and music are generated by code, so they have the rough, honest charm of that approach — and most of the game itself was written with Claude.

card.title: The Elevator Algorithm
card.excerpt: A browser game for algorithmic thinking: write a JavaScript controller, run it against a deterministic elevator sim, and iterate until riders wait less.

cover.title: The Elevator Algorithm
cover.lede: Standing in line on a summer trip to Universal Orlando, I started wondering what algorithm actually runs an elevator. This is the answer turned into a game: you write a JavaScript controller, run it against a deterministic simulation, and watch it drive the building — then iterate across levels that get harder one idea at a time.
cover.note: It teaches the why, not the answer. Reference controllers (FCFS, SSTF, SCAN, LOOK) sit behind a clearly labeled spoilers panel, and hints name the idea and the symptom in your own run rather than hand you the solution.
